candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items); this item tests case management, referrals, discharge planning, and continuity across care settings.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Case management and continuity across inpatient, outpatient, and community rehabilitation
candidate.educational_objective: Use case management to coordinate early multidisciplinary discharge planning, referrals, follow-up, and a clear post-discharge contact for clients with complex traumatic brain injury rehabilitation needs.

options.A: Coordinate an early multidisciplinary discharge plan, document follow-up and referrals, and identify who will be the client's key contact after discharge
options.B: Wait until the day of discharge before contacting community rehabilitation services
options.C: End coordination once the client leaves the hospital because outpatient rehabilitation should develop an unrelated plan
options.D: Limit discharge planning to insurance authorization and omit rehabilitation goals, follow-up, and community providers

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NICE rehabilitation guidance recommends early multidisciplinary discharge planning for people with complex rehabilitation needs after traumatic injury, reassessment of needs before discharge, coordinated and integrated support during transition to outpatient/community services, documentation of how rehabilitation will continue, and a defined point of contact or key contact after discharge when ongoing needs remain. These recommendations apply to traumatic injuries including brain injury. B delays coordination. C creates fragmentation across settings. D reduces case management to administrative authorization and omits the clinical continuity functions specified by the guideline.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NICE guidance directly supports early multidisciplinary discharge planning, integrated transition across services, documented follow-up/referrals, and a defined post-discharge contact for people with complex traumatic-injury rehabilitation needs.
candidate.source_locator: NICE NG211 → Section 1.8 'Coordination of rehabilitation care at discharge': Recommendation 1.8.1 early multidisciplinary discharge planning; 1.8.2 reassess needs/review rehabilitation plan before discharge; 1.8.14 coordinated, consistent, integrated multidisciplinary approach through transfer to outpatient services; 1.8.15 document ongoing support, referrals and review appointments in rehabilitation plan/handover; 1.8.21–1.8.22 provide a single point of contact and agree a key contact when ongoing rehabilitation/health/social-care support is needed.
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
candidate.source_version_date: NICE guideline NG211 published 2022-01-18; current guidance accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A client with a significant traumatic brain injury will need ongoing rehabilitation and social-care services after hospital discharge. Which case-management action best supports continuity of care?
